newsitem.title: BRAZIL: ADP Inc acquires control of ADP Brazil.
newsitem.headline: ADP Inc acquires control of ADP Brazil.

text.p: U.S. computer service company Automatic Data Processing Inc (ADP) reached a deal with Brazil's RBS media group to acquire 95-percent control of its local associate, an official said Thursday.
"Before the agreement, ADP owned 14 percent of the firm and RBS held 84 percent," said Christye Cantero, a spokeswoman for ADP Brazil, adding RBS will retain five percent of the company.
She said the total value of the deal was not given.
In a statement, ADP Brazil said the accord was in keeping with the strategies of both RBS and ADP in the United States.
The expansion of its presence in Brazil is part of ADP's international expansion plans, it said.
In addition to North America, the firm has a strong presence in Europe and has now begun paving the way for further growth in Latin America.
"Brazil is the world's ninth-largest economy and has become the platform for our future development on the (South American) continent," ADP group President Gary Butler said in the statement.
Other target countries in the region are Argentina, Chile and Venezuela, the statement said.
Meanwhile, RBS has decided to focus on television, cable TV, broadcasting and the Internet in order to consolidate its efforts on multimedia in southern Brazil.
The statement said Brazil's new economic stability and single-digit inflation were two factors that led ADP to assume control of the local firm.
The new U.S. parent plans to double ADP Brazil's annual receipts of more than $60 million as well as its 2,500 clients, it said.
Worldwide, the company last year had costs of $200 million apart from $250 million set aside for the purchase of products and companies.
ADP Brazil's general manager, Luiz Henrique Saraiva Pereira, said the change in ownership at his firm will intensify the existing interchange with ADP in the United States.
"With this new shareholding arrangement, the synergy will grow in the area of technology, easing the availability of new products In the local market," he was quoted as saying.
